## Distinct parallel lines or the same line? {#fv4-coincident .fv-lesson .relation-lesson }

```{=html}
<p>The direction vectors are scalar multiples. <strong>Must these be the same line?</strong></p><div data-parallel-lines></div>
```

<div class="booklet-cue">Booklet §3.3 · pp. 51–52 · Additional illustration</div>

::: {.notes}
Use a short prediction before changing the fixed point. The fixed line is $\ell_1:\ \underset{\sim}{r}=\begin{bmatrix}1\\2\end{bmatrix}+\lambda\begin{bmatrix}2\\1\end{bmatrix}$. The other line has a parallel direction and independent parameter $\mu$. Keep the explanation geometric: when its fixed point B is off the first line, the lines are distinct and parallel; when B is on the first line, the lines coincide. The dashed green line overlays the blue line in the coincident state. Ask: “What information did the direction vectors give us, and what extra information did the position of B give us?” Distinct parallel lines have no common point; coincident lines share every point. Save the point-testing calculation for the dedicated worked demonstration on the next slide. The buttons are touch-sized and Reset restores the distinct-lines state. No camera rotation or simultaneous-parameter solving is required.
:::
